diagrams.title: **Six things that make memory hard
diagrams.caption: **Six things that make memory hard.** Every managed memory service you'll meet, including AgentCore Memory, is essentially a set of answers to these six.
diagrams.svg:
<svg viewBox="0 0 1100 400" aria-label="Six challenges of agent memory: storage scalability, memory refresh, integration complexity, privacy and security, retrieval accuracy, and observability." style="max-width:100%;height:auto;display:block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
      <g>
        <rect x="20" y="20" width="340" height="170" rx="18" class="bx2" style="fill:#F8F9FC;stroke:#2958C4;stroke-width:2.5"></rect>
        <path d="M44 60 V110 A30 9 0 0 0 104 110 V60" class="data" style="fill:#E1E9FC;stroke:#2958C4;stroke-width:2.5"></path><ellipse cx="74" cy="60" rx="30" ry="9" class="data" style="fill:#E1E9FC;stroke:#2958C4;stroke-width:2.5"></ellipse><path d="M44 85 A30 9 0 0 0 104 85" fill="none" stroke="#2958C4" stroke-width="2"></path>
        <text x="124" y="70" class="t" style="font-family:'Plus Jakarta Sans', sans-serif;fill:#19203F;font-size:19px;font-weight:700">1 Storage</text><text x="124" y="96" class="t" style="font-family:'Plus Jakarta Sans', sans-serif;fill:#19203F;font-size:19px;font-weight:700">scalability</text>
        <text x="44" y="150" class="ts" style="font-family:'Plus Jakarta Sans', sans-serif;fill:#586082;font-size:16px;font-weight:400">Memory grows fast; millions of</text><text x="44" y="172" class="ts" style="font-family:'Plus Jakarta Sans', sans-serif;fill:#586082;font-size:16px;font-weight:400">embeddings are costly to keep fast</text>
      </g>
      <g>
        <rect x="380" y="20" width="340" height="170" rx="18" class="bx2" style="fill:#F8F9FC;stroke:#0B7F73;stroke-width:2.5"></rect>
        <path d="M434 62 A26 26 0 1 1 410 92" fill="none" stroke="#0B7F73" stroke-width="5" stroke-linecap="round"></path><path d="M426 52 L436 62 L424 70" fill="none" stroke="#0B7F73" stroke-width="5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"></path>
        <text x="484" y="70" class="t" style="font-family:'Plus Jakarta Sans', sans-serif;fill:#19203F;font-size:19px;font-weight:700">2 Memory</text><text x="484" y="96" class="t" style="font-family:'Plus Jakarta Sans', sans-serif;fill:#19203F;font-size:19px;font-weight:700">refresh</text>
        <text x="404" y="150" class="ts" style="font-family:'Plus Jakarta Sans', sans-serif;fill:#586082;font-size:16px;font-weight:400">Facts change; what to keep,</text><text x="404" y="172" class="ts" style="font-family:'Plus Jakarta Sans', sans-serif;fill:#586082;font-size:16px;font-weight:400">update or forget?</text>
      </g>
      <g>
        <rect x="740" y="20" width="340" height="170" rx="18" class="bx2" style="fill:#F8F9FC;stroke:#6C43CC;stroke-width:2.5"></rect>
        <rect x="764" y="56" width="34" height="34" rx="8" class="proto" style="fill:#ECE5FC;stroke:#6C43CC;stroke-width:2.5"></rect><rect x="814" y="80" width="34" height="34" rx="8" class="proto" style="fill:#ECE5FC;stroke:#6C43CC;stroke-width:2.5"></rect><path d="M798 73 H814 M831 90 V80" stroke="#6C43CC" stroke-width="3"></path>
        <text x="864" y="70" class="t" style="font-family:'Plus Jakarta Sans', sans-serif;fill:#19203F;font-size:19px;font-weight:700">3 Integration</text><text x="864" y="96" class="t" style="font-family:'Plus Jakarta Sans', sans-serif;fill:#19203F;font-size:19px;font-weight:700">complexity</text>
        <text x="764" y="150" class="ts" style="font-family:'Plus Jakarta Sans', sans-serif;fill:#586082;font-size:16px;font-weight:400">LLM + vector DBs + APIs + layers</text><text x="764" y="172" class="ts" style="font-family:'Plus Jakarta Sans', sans-serif;fill:#586082;font-size:16px;font-weight:400">of memory, all in real time</text>
      </g>
      <g>
        <rect x="20" y="210" width="340" height="170" rx="18" class="bx2" style="fill:#F8F9FC;stroke:#C4344F;stroke-width:2.5"></rect>
        <rect x="48" y="262" width="52" height="40" rx="8" class="risk" style="fill:#FBE3E8;stroke:#C4344F;stroke-width:2.5"></rect><path d="M58 262 V250 A16 16 0 0 1 90 250 V262" fill="none" stroke="#C4344F" stroke-width="5"></path>
        <text x="124" y="260" class="t" style="font-family:'Plus Jakarta Sans', sans-serif;fill:#19203F;font-size:19px;font-weight:700">4 Privacy and</text><text x="124" y="286" class="t" style="font-family:'Plus Jakarta Sans', sans-serif;fill:#19203F;font-size:19px;font-weight:700">security</text>
        <text x="44" y="340" class="ts" style="font-family:'Plus Jakarta Sans', sans-serif;fill:#586082;font-size:16px;font-weight:400">Personal data is a target; one user's</text><text x="44" y="362" class="ts" style="font-family:'Plus Jakarta Sans', sans-serif;fill:#586082;font-size:16px;font-weight:400">memory must never leak to another</text>
      </g>
      <g>
        <rect x="380" y="210" width="340" height="170" rx="18" class="bx2" style="fill:#F8F9FC;stroke:#B07600;stroke-width:2.5"></rect>
        <circle cx="430" cy="270" r="22" fill="none" stroke="#B07600" stroke-width="5"></circle><path d="M446 286 L466 306" stroke="#B07600" stroke-width="7" stroke-linecap="round"></path>
        <text x="484" y="260" class="t" style="font-family:'Plus Jakarta Sans', sans-serif;fill:#19203F;font-size:19px;font-weight:700">5 Retrieval</text><text x="484" y="286" class="t" style="font-family:'Plus Jakarta Sans', sans-serif;fill:#19203F;font-size:19px;font-weight:700">accuracy</text>
        <text x="404" y="340" class="ts" style="font-family:'Plus Jakarta Sans', sans-serif;fill:#586082;font-size:16px;font-weight:400">Finding exactly the right memory,</text><text x="404" y="362" class="ts" style="font-family:'Plus Jakarta Sans', sans-serif;fill:#586082;font-size:16px;font-weight:400">not noisy half-matches</text>
      </g>
      <g>
        <rect x="740" y="210" width="340" height="170" rx="18" class="bx2" style="fill:#F8F9FC;stroke:#4A5170;stroke-width:2.5"></rect>
        <path d="M762 296 A36 36 0 0 1 834 296" fill="none" stroke="#4A5170" stroke-width="5"></path><path d="M798 296 L820 270" stroke="#4A5170" stroke-width="4" stroke-linecap="round"></path><circle cx="798" cy="296" r="5" class="fill-user" style="fill:#4A5170"></circle>
        <text x="864" y="260" class="t" style="font-family:'Plus Jakarta Sans', sans-serif;fill:#19203F;font-size:19px;font-weight:700">6 Observability</text>
        <text x="764" y="340" class="ts" style="font-family:'Plus Jakarta Sans', sans-serif;fill:#586082;font-size:16px;font-weight:400">Why did it remember that? Why</text><text x="764" y="362" class="ts" style="font-family:'Plus Jakarta Sans', sans-serif;fill:#586082;font-size:16px;font-weight:400">did it miss this? Hard to see</text>
      </g>
    </svg>

diagrams.title: **Read, think, answer, write
diagrams.caption: **Read, think, answer, write.** Solid arrows 2 and 3 read memory before thinking; dashed arrows 6 write back afterwards, so the next request starts smarter.

Four: it combines everything into a prompt for the LLM. Five: it produces a response or action. diagrams.title: **One brain, several kinds of memory
diagrams.caption: **One brain, several kinds of memory.** The LLM sits in the middle; each memory store answers a different question ("what was just said?", "what are the facts?", "what is this similar to?"), and the orchestration layer decides which to ask.
diagrams.svg:
<svg class="dimmable" viewBox="0 0 1100 600" aria-label="Choices for implementing memory on AWS. At the centre, the LLM service: Amazon Bedrock or Amazon SageMaker AI. Short-term memory: Amazon DynamoDB, Redis, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Memory. Long-term structured memory: Amazon Aurora, Amazon DynamoDB, Amazon Neptune. Durable storage: Amazon S3. Long-term semantic memory: Amazon OpenSearch, PostgreSQL with pgvector, Pinecone, Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases. Memory orchestration: LangGraph, AWS Lambda, AWS Step Functions, Strands Agents SDK. Seven numbered steps show a question flowing through orchestration, the memory stores and the LLM." style="max-width:100%;height:auto;display:block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><defs><marker id="ah" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5" markerWidth="7" markerHeight="7" orient="auto-start-reverse"><path class="ah" d="M0,0 L10,5 L0,10 z"></path></marker></defs>

diagrams.title: **Graph databases follow relationships
diagrams.caption: **Graph databases follow relationships.** The answer is whoever is linked to *both* nodes. A relational database can do this with joins; a graph database makes it the natural question to ask.

diagrams.title: **Nodes and edges
diagrams.caption: **Nodes and edges.** Each node is one step (call the LLM, execute a tool, retrieve memory, apply business logic). Edges control the flow, including loops, conditional branches and retries. You'll build exactly this loop in the second lab.
